 ## Search results
Multi-negative softmax is a plausible objective-only intervention for NextItNet: its original paper explicitly supports sampled-softmax training without changing the causal convolution backbone ([NextItNet](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf)). The 2024 study [On the Effectiveness of Sampled Softmax](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) identifies implicit hard-negative mining and connections to ranking metrics; temperature controls how strongly high-scoring negatives dominate. [Scalable Cross-Entropy, RecSys 2024](https://dspace.mit.edu/entities/publication/5392aca9-0bae-4176-9b3a-a8165957ba26) approximates full-catalog CE through GPU-efficient selection of informative outputs. These support comparing multiple negatives against the existing single-negative objective while retaining one network and scoring head; they do not establish gains on this benchmark.

Harder negatives introduce false-negative risk. [PSL, NeurIPS 2024](https://zhoushengisnoob.github.io/papers/NIPS24_PSL.pdf) shows that softmax’s exponential weighting can overemphasize false negatives and proposes alternative pairwise surrogate activations. A tractable experimental hypothesis is sampled CE with 16–64 uniform negatives, followed separately by a uniform/semi-hard mixture or PSL; exclude padding, targets and observed training positives, and tune temperature before adding aggressive mining. Keep architecture and training budget fixed and select by macro validation HR@10. More negatives are not automatically better: a [2026 preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11061) reports that larger batches with fewer negatives can outperform the reverse under a fixed memory budget, motivating measurement of both ranking quality and throughput.

---

Search found related mechanisms, but no verified 2023–2026 NextItNet paper establishing input-dependent causal resets. [NextItNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163) supplies the relevant backbone: stacked causal dilated convolutions with residual connections. [TimeWeaver (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-8954/13/10/857) describes gated fusion of convolutional features from different receptive fields; this supports adaptive context weighting, but does not establish that stale information disappears from the complete residual network. [ConvRec (2026)](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2026/284) explores hierarchical convolution for attribute-aware recommendation, rather than input-dependent forgetting.

The clearest transferable mechanism is [ADCNN (2022)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0031320321005495): input-conditioned, position-specific dilation selection using Gumbel-Softmax. Its evidence concerns spatial vision, so causal sequential recommendation remains an adaptation hypothesis. [SRF-Net (2021)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.15258) similarly adapts temporal receptive fields at individual locations. Both motivate jointly trained internal convolution controls within one NextItNet model; neither demonstrates recommendation-specific intent resets.

Proposed experiment, inferred from these mechanisms: gate individual causal convolution taps using current and source features, or suppress taps crossing learned intent boundaries. Apply controls throughout the stack: shrinking a later receptive field cannot remove old context already encoded in its inputs, and residual bypasses can preserve that context. Verify forgetting through complete-output interventions: hold the recent suffix fixed, replace or delete progressively older prefixes, and measure candidate-score changes and top-10 overlap. Report these alongside macro validation HR@10 and an ungated ablation. Gate values alone establish neither forgetting nor recommendation benefit.

---

Related 2023–2026 research supports text–behavior alignment, but the retrieved papers do not establish the exact combination of a jointly trained, randomly initialized text encoder, removable auxiliary branch, and unchanged NextItNet inference. [ADRec (2025)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0950705125003375) aligns sequence and target-item text representations using supervised and self-supervised contrastive signals.
